title: Antoine Moses Sets Guinness Record: 47,460 Mangroves Planted in 24 Hours at Mombasa Tudor Creek
detail: Environmentalist Antoine Moses completed a 24-hour mangrove restoration marathon at the Mirarani Site in Tudor Creek, Mombasa County, Kenya on May 1, 2026, setting a new Guinness World Record by planting 47,460 mangrove propagules in a single day. The historic event was hosted by Kenya's State Department for Forestry in coordination with the Kenya Forest Service, EarthLungs Reforestation Foundation, Veritree, Mombasa County Government, and local coastal communities. The initiative directly supports Kenya's flagship 15 Billion Tree Growing Programme, which targets a dramatic national increase in tree and forest cover by 2032. Mangroves offer exceptional climate value — storing up to four times more carbon per hectare than tropical rainforests — while providing coastal storm protection, fisheries nursery habitat, and livelihoods for Kenya's coastal communities. Kenya has legally protected all 61,000 hectares of its mangrove coverage since 2017.

title: Minnesota: 40,000 Seedlings Planted at Munger Shaw Fire Site in First Reforestation Phase
detail: On May 1, 2026, the St. Louis County Land and Minerals Forestry Division launched active reforestation of areas burned by the Munger Shaw wildfire. Minnesota Power donated 23,000 pine seedlings, complemented by 17,000 seedlings from county nursery stock, with a mix of red pine and white pine planted across 48 acres of tax-forfeited burned land. Approximately 350,000 seedlings are planned for planting throughout 2026 across all fire-affected areas. Foresters observed encouraging signs of natural aspen regeneration at some sites. The effort is part of Minnesota's broader spring 2026 reforestation campaign, which included the Minnesota DNR planting nearly 2 million seedlings on state forest land across the state.
